sources: STS-81 Space Shuttle Mission Report: Table I (SRB ignition 012:09:27:22.984, MECO 09:35:55, ET separation 09:36:14, OMS-2 TIG 10:10:23.3); Missions Summary NASA/TM-2011-216142 p. 2-98 (MECO VI 25,922 actual / 25,915 predicted, MECO cmd 8:29.9, 104/104/109%, ET-83 LWT, post OMS-2 159.9 x 84.9 nmi, launch window 6m59s, Mir planar/phase window)
Mir's plane: the element set of 1997-01-12T06:22:16 UTC from S16609.txt (tools/mir_elements.py), inclination 51.6721 deg
Everything else as sts135-dolilu.json, which is as sts134-dolilu.json: STS-81 is flown first as a cross-check flight
notes: A CROSS-CHECK FLIGHT, as STS-135: the vehicle model and first-stage tables were built for STS-134; flown with them to see which differences from the real flight are the model's.  The first run will show how far the yaw, pitch and throttle tables are off; retune by flight.

IYD: MIR's plane at SRB ignition LEADING by the J2 regression the lower Orbiter will have gained by Ti (NODE_LEAD_DEG in make_sts081_flight.py; --node-lead 0 for Mir's plane as it was), Earth-fixed: inclination 51.6721 deg, node 256.2618 deg east (RAAN of date less GMST); IYD = (-sin i sin node, sin i cos node, -cos i), the form sts134/135's use.  The pad (39B) is 1.06 deg off this plane at SRB ignition and in plane at 1997 day 12 GMT 09:34:06 (T_GMTLO_REF), about 403 s later: the flown launch was at the opening of the 6m59s planar window, so the window closed about when the pad passed through the plane.

MASSES: the Space Shuttle Missions Summary's Appendix A-6 weight table (pdf page 278), STS-81 row: orbiter 250167 lb at SRB ignition (242,178 at insertion), ET 1,663,879 lb, SRB 1,298,753 lb, shuttle total 4,511,011 lb.  The first run used an estimate of 242,000 lb and MECO came 7 s early.

Message 11, the wind table: Jacksonville's (72206) balloon of 1997-01-11 23:04Z, the last before liftoff -- Cape Canaveral's 74794 is not in the archive for 1997, and Jacksonville is the nearest east-coast station that is.  The truth flies the 23:04Z and 11:03Z profiles blended to 09:27Z (sts081-sounding-72206-19970112-0927Z.csv, weight 0.87 on the later).
OMS 2: TIG = ET separation + 2049.3 s (ET sep 09:36:14, OMS-2 10:10:23.3); pre-flight targets are placeholders -- the ground designs them after MECO for 159.9 x 84.9 nmi (75.5 ft/s flown).

fields.name: PSI(1-30): the tape's 38-deg table turned by -28.71 deg: -18.71 for the inertial azimuth (63.66 -> 44.95), and -10 found by flight -- the first stage then ends 18 nmi out of the final plane instead of 29, the MECO target is reached (-18 and -26 fall short) (PSI = tan(yaw/4), GG31ST.hal step 16)

THET(1,1-30), tan(theta/4): shaped by flight to STS-134's ASCENT ADI - NOMINAL cue card (Ascent Checklist CC 10-11, ASC-14a/134; the same on every OI-34 flight's card): pitch 69/62/52/39/30 deg, H 10/27/51/85/126 kft, Hdot 670/1007/1441/1902/2200 ft/s at T+30/50/70/90/110. Flight p10: 70.1/63.3/56.1/38.9/29.3 deg, 8.9/25.8/49.9/84.3/126.4 kft, 646/1001/1460/1928/2226 ft/s; max-q 716 psf (STS-134: 733.1 at T+60); second stage within ~5 kft of the card from Vi 10,000 on. THET is applied before the yaw turn and load relief takes several degrees at max-q, so it runs well above the flown pitch (to 78.8 deg near Vrel 1,280). Was the tape's table with the pitch-over scaled 0.88 (max-q ~950 psf).
PHI(1-15): the same turn at liftoff (PHI(1) = PSI(1): no roll on the pad), blended out by heads-down 180 deg
QPOLY(1-4): Vrel at STS-81's flown throttle times T+4.2, 31.1, 60.7 s (Mission Report Table I) on the simulated vehicle
TREF_ADJUST: guidance saw 488 ft/s at T+20.73 in flight sts135a (TREF 21.0 gave TDEL -0.27 s and a 68% bucket: 72 + 6000 x -0.27 / 405)
THROT(1-4): 104, 70 (the flown max-q bucket, Table I), 104, 104
GAMD 0.65 deg, as the tape reconfiguration's FPA_NOM (sts134-reconfig.json)
